correctness.rationale: The negative-pool probability follows from a beta integral: \(Q_k=(\tau-a)_k/(\tau)_k\). The adjacent difference is \(C_{k+1}-C_k=(R_k-1)/[k(k+1)]\), with \(R_{k+1}/R_k=1+[(1-a)k+2(\tau-a)]/[k(\tau+k+1)]>1\) for \(0<a<\min\{1,\tau\}\). Gamma-ratio asymptotics imply \(R_k\to\infty\), proving at most one sign crossing and at most one adjacent minimum tie. At \(a=\tau p\downarrow0\), a uniformly bounded second-order error in the logarithm of the beta product and comparison at \(k=\lfloor c/a\rfloor\) prove \(R_k\to c\) and hence \(a k_*\to1\). Digamma harmonic sums yield the exact minimum \(a[\log(1/a)+1-\psi(\tau)]+o(a)\). The independent benchmark follows from \(k=\Theta(p^{-1/2})\) and the limiting convex cost. The bundled checker verified 168 exact rational adjacent identities and rational optima at \(p=1/20,1/100,1/1000\); finite checking is not the asymptotic proof.

value.rationale: For disease screening with fixed positive within-pool correlation, \(k_*\sim1/(\tau p)\), whereas independent screening has \(k_*\sim p^{-1/2}\). The minimal assay costs scale respectively like \(\tau p\log(1/p)\) and \(2\sqrt p\), with an explicitly proved second-order term \(\tau p[1-\log\tau-\psi(\tau)]\). These are qualitatively different asymptotic regimes with identifiable assumptions and constants, not a small numeric improvement or arbitrary slice. The monotone adjacent ratio yields an exact integer design threshold. Unlimited pools may be impractical because of dilution, clustered population sizes, and variable assay costs.
